user_scenario: You are Margit Oyelaran, controller of Kestrel Ridge Tool & Die Inc., the machine shop at 3150 Lakeshore Industrial Dr in Spring Lake, Michigan. You are calling Lakeshore Power & Light from the plant office, organised and a little pressed for time, with the company's utility folder open in front of you. You know the company paid Lakeshore a cash security deposit on the plant's electric account two years ago, and you know the plant's electric bills have roughly doubled since the second production line started running this spring. You open by saying you are calling about the security deposit on the Spring Lake plant's account: if Lakeshore needs more deposit from Kestrel Ridge, you would like to pay whatever part of it is due, today, on this call, rather than wait for a letter. You are authorised to act for the company, you are happy for the representative to record whatever Lakeshore's rules require on the deposit, and you will make any deposit payment yourself. When the representative asks how to find the account, you give the company's phone number on file, 6164307259. Only when the representative asks you to verify the account do you give the last four digits of the company's EIN, 5138; if one more detail is wanted you give the billing email, ap@kestrelridgetool.com, or the billing ZIP code, 49456. You do not know Lakeshore's deposit rules, figures or internal steps and you never suggest an amount, a date or a number of installments. If the representative tells you the deposit cannot be returned yet or that its review is being pushed back, you take it in stride, saying the plant did pay a few bills late during the expansion, and that is fine. If the representative mentions interest being added to the deposit, you say that is good to hear. If the representative offers to take a surety bond or a letter of credit instead of cash, you say the company will keep the deposit in cash. If the representative asks how the company will pay, you say from the company's operating account. If the representative explains that the required deposit is going up, you ask how much has to be paid today and you accept the plan as the representative describes it. When the representative hands the deposit payment over to you, you make it yourself exactly as set out to you — the deposit reference, the installment number, the number of installments and the amount — and once the payment shows as received you thank the representative and end the call.

edges.condition: The deposit's status is assessed while it keeps a fully_secured_date on record, and its required_amount is the recalculated requirement, above the held cash.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the deposit is still held and its recorded required amount is the 5785.00 set at the 2025 recalculation, equal to the held cash of 5785.00; it has not returned to assessed status and shows no raised requirement, so there is no additional amount an installment can be worked out from.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The recalculation write at step 14 sets status assessed, required_amount 13694.00, average_monthly_bill 7020.11 and due date 2026-10-17 while fully_secured_date 2024-10-07 stays on record, so the deposit shows a raised requirement in assessed status.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The anniversaries of the fully secured date 2024-10-07 reached by 2026-10-07 are 2025-10-07 and 2026-10-07; the deposit carries only one interest credit, whose period ends 2025-10-07, so the anniversary reached today has no interest credit.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The interest write at step 12 books a deposit_interest_credit of 119.61 with interest_period_end 2026-10-07, raising the held amount read by the phase-in from 6207.60 to 6327.21.

edges.condition: The deposit's refund_review_date is later than the anniversary whose year is being credited, which is the day the credit is booked.
edges.policy_source: The interest for a completed year is credited only once the refund review date recorded on the deposit falls after the anniversary that closes that year.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The refund review date recorded on the deposit is 2026-10-07, the very anniversary being credited, so it does not fall after that anniversary.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain additional installment -> recalculated requirement -> anniversary interest -> review extension; every problem has exactly one prerequisite and no problem has two parallel prerequisites, so the only topological order is extension (step 10), interest (step 12), recalculation (step 14), installment (step 16). Each later write reads the effect of the earlier one: the interest sentence 'The interest for a completed year is credited only once the refund review date recorded on the deposit falls after the anniversary that closes that year.', the recalculation sentence 'The recalculated requirement is not fixed until the deposit carries an interest credit for every anniversary of its fully secured date reached so far.' and the installment sentence 'The installment of an additional deposit is worked out only after the deposit shows its raised required amount and has returned to assessed status.' pin the order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the recalculation write leaves required_amount 5785.00 in held status; the installment then computes to 0.00 (additional amount due floored at zero against the held basis 6327.21) instead of 2946.70, and the terminal deposit stays held with no raised requirement.
Skipping the interest write leaves the held amount at 6207.60; the phased recalculated requirement becomes 13634.00 instead of 13694.00, and the terminal ledger lacks the 119.61 interest credit.

Skipping the extension write leaves refund_review_date at 2026-10-07 instead of 2026-12-07 in the terminal state, and the interest credit would be booked while the recorded review date does not fall after the anniversary it closes.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only paying whatever additional deposit is due today. It never mentions the satisfactory payment review or its date, interest on the deposit, or a recalculation of the requirement, and contains no hint that something must be sorted out first; the lines about the review being pushed back and interest being added are passive reactions that fire only after the representative says so.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: None of the four tools checks a prerequisite: extend_deposit_review_04d6c850 only shifts the recorded review date by the months given; credit_deposit_interest_e2c6de3a only books the interest credit and raises held_amount; require_additional_deposit_b541b477 only overwrites required_amount, average_monthly_bill, first_installment_due_date, assessed_date and status; pay_additional_deposit_64b1dc0d only books the payment and records the installment count. Each runs and writes even when its prerequisite is unmet (for example pay_additional_deposit_64b1dc0d would book a payment against a deposit still in held status), returning a normal receipt with no Error and no hint.

seed_consistency.check: Medium Commercial Service Deposit on the Schedule GD agreement, assessed 2024-09-27 for late payment history: the second late payment charge in 12 months (GD late_payment_trigger_count 2) was posted 2024-09-05, so the assessment fell inside the 30-day window. Assessed at deposit_multiple_of_average_bill 2.5 times the 4246.55 mean of the 12 regular bills 2023-10-15..2024-09-15 = 10616.38, rounded up to 10617.00; paid in one installment on its due date 2024-10-07, which became the fully secured date, so the refund review date is 2024-10-07 plus 24 months = 2026-10-07. The 2025-10-07 recalculation lowered the requirement to 5785.00 on a basis of 3305.37 (excess 4832.00 refunded by check), so required_amount 5785.00, average_monthly_bill 3305.37 and held_amount 10617.00 - 4832.00 + 422.60 = 6207.60 are consistent.
Single cash payment of the full 10617.00 requirement as installment 1 on 2024-10-07 while the deposit was assessed; it made the deposit held that day.

First-anniversary credit 422.60 for 2024-10-07..2025-10-07 under the interest law: 85 days of 2024 at rate_2024 0.0385 and 280 days of 2025 at rate_2025 0.0402 over 365 on the 10617.00 cash received, no late charge counted in that year so 12 months earned.

Excess refund by check on 2025-10-07: the 12-month recalculation on the 3305.37 mean, a clean record (multiple 2.0) less 0.25 for 76 months of service, gave 5785.00 below the held cash 10617.00, so 4832.00 was refunded and the deposit stayed held.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — security_deposits task 0 (Kestrel Ridge Tool & Die Inc., Medium Commercial Service Deposit).

0. DRAW AND SCOPE SNAPSHOT. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 5, 4]}; --tasks 2 showed task 1 = {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 6]}. Task 0 is the first task, so nothing was occupied. Claimed here (whole tree): deposit_ext_failed_review_extension (5 factors, tool extend_deposit_review_04d6c850, agent), deposit_ext_anniversary_interest (4 factors, credit_deposit_interest_e2c6de3a, agent), deposit_ext_recalculated_requirement (5 factors, require_additional_deposit_b541b477, agent), deposit_ext_additional_installment (5 factors, pay_additional_deposit_64b1dc0d, owner=user). Reserved headroom for task 1 (3 problems, 4/4/6 factors): the assessment of a deposit on a new agreement pending start (deposit_assessment), the opening installment of a new agreement's deposit (deposit_payment through a different user tool) and the full refund of a deposit on a passed review (deposit_refund_completion + deposit_refund by check). None of those tools is touched here; task 1's tree (refund and opening installment as parallel prerequisites of the new-agreement assessment) shares no policy with this one, and the families stay separate: the review extension, anniversary interest, recalculation and additional installment belong to this task alone.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The customer asks only to pay whatever additional deposit is due today. Nothing is due at the opening: the deposit is held with required_amount 5785.00. To reach the payment the agent must read out of the policies that (a) the deposit's 24-month review falls today and is NOT passed (three counted late charges against an allowance of two once the 2025-11-05 courtesy waiver is deducted), whose outcome is a review-date extension; (b) the interest policy books the year's interest only once the review date has moved past the anniversary; (c) the recalculation waits on that interest credit because a rise driven by load growth is phased in against the held amount, which includes credited interest; (d) the installment waits on the raised requirement in assessed status. Each hop is a numeric write with its own 4-5 factor computation over a 36-bill, 6-late-charge, 3-row deposit ledger history. Difficulty comes from discovering the chain and reconciling history, never from picking among similar tools (each problem has exactly one tool).

2. BLUEPRINT DEFECTS ROUTED AROUND (blueprint frozen; recorded here). (i) The difficulty claim lists event_types without deposit_interest_credit and deposit_additional_requirement although its summary names deposit_interest_rule and deposit_recalculation as this difficulty's governing rules and no other difficulty claims those events; this difficulty uses them for the interest and recalculation problems. (ii) deposit_installments_and_security's dedup gate 'Each installment number is recorded once.' binds deposit_transactions.installment_number to the call, but a new installment number exists in no pre-action record, so the structured gate can never be evidenced; the additional-installment policy declares an overwrite of that sentence with its own numbering rule ('numbered on from the deposit's latest installment number, so that no installment number is recorded twice'), which keeps the dedup meaning in prose.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root = deposit_ext_additional_installment (the customer's 'pay whatever part of it is due'). Chain, no parallel edges:
 E1 additional_installment -> recalculated_requirement: kind value_input, gate binding raised_requirement (F('required_amount')), form state. Prerequisite sentence (affirmative, own rule): 'The installment of an additional deposit is worked out only after the deposit shows its raised required amount and has returned to assessed status.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state (status assessed + raised required_amount, with fully_secured_date on record); no tool/id/code token; strength exact (hard 'only after', the one state). Exactly one write of this difficulty brings a held deposit back to assessed with a raised requirement: require_additional_deposit_b541b477 (the new-agreement assessment of task 1 creates a deposit with no fully secured date, so it does not produce this state). Opening evidence: deposit_accounts.a0ce5ba0-f127-40c9-a1ce-a8cf8a0ba3cc.status = held, required_amount = 5785.0. Flip: step 14 sets assessed / 13694.00. Deletion run: skipping step 14 gives installment 0.00 instead of 2946.70.
 E2 recalculated_requirement -> anniversary_interest: kind value_input, gate binding held_amount_now, form state. Sentence (negated direction, own rule): 'The recalculated requirement is not fixed until the deposit carries an interest credit for every anniversary of its fully secured date reached so far.' Connective 'not ... until'; record-visible state (deposit_interest_credit rows with interest_period_end on each anniversary); no code token; exact scope 'every anniversary ... reached so far'. Only credit_deposit_interest_e2c6de3a writes interest credits in this difficulty. Opening evidence: deposit_transactions.6b1b34ec-1a43-43b1-804a-a54fad93ffd9.interest_period_end = 2025-10-07 (none for 2026-10-07). Flip: step 12 books 119.61 ending 2026-10-07. Deletion run: skipping step 12 gives 13634.00 instead of 13694.00.
 E3 anniversary_interest -> failed_review_extension: kind state_gate, gate deposit_accounts.refund_review_date, form state. Sentence (affirmative, own rule): 'The interest for a completed year is credited only once the refund review date recorded on the deposit falls after the anniversary that closes that year.' Connective 'only once'; record-visible field; no code token. Only extend_deposit_review_04d6c850 moves a recorded review date. Opening evidence: deposit_accounts.a0ce5ba0-f127-40c9-a1ce-a8cf8a0ba3cc.refund_review_date = 2026-10-07 (equal to the anniversary). Flip: step 10 moves it to 2026-12-07. Deletion run: terminal refund_review_date stays 2026-10-07.
 Derivations: sentence + records + depended-on rule -> one action in each case (the recalculation rule says it 'returns to assessed with the new required amount'; the interest rule says it books 'one interest credit ... whose period ends on the anniversary'; the extension rule says the review date 'moves out ... by a whole number of calendar months'). value_input edges = 2 >= max(3-1,1). Topological order V(10) -> I(12) -> R(14) -> P(16) is the only one. The charter's prerequisite sentences run in both directions (affirmative for the interest credit and the installment, negated for the recalculated figure), each chosen as that desk would state it. user_scenario names no review, interest or recalculation (passive reactions only). Tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Step 10 subject deposit_review_update: governing deposit_refund_review (its only gate review_date_reached applies to deposit_refund_completion, so policy_scope); the review is decided on its date 2026-10-07 = frozen date; base 'The review passes when ... no more than refund_max_late_payments' fails: counted 3 > 2. Step 12 subject deposit_interest_credit: deposit_interest_rule gate interest_on_held_deposit ('Each interest period is credited once, and interest is credited only on a deposit in held status.') — status held at the opening and still held after step 10; period ending 2026-10-07 not yet credited (latest ends 2025-10-07); correlation deposit_accounts.deposit_id = a0ce5ba0-f127-40c9-a1ce-a8cf8a0ba3cc. Step 14 subject deposit_additional_requirement: deposit_recalculation (no structured gate; policy_scope): recalculated every 12 months after 2024-10-07, so due 2026-10-07; 13694.00 exceeds the held cash 5785.00 by 136.7% > recalculation_increase_threshold_pct 0.20; due within additional_deposit_due_days 10 -> 2026-10-17. Step 16 subject deposit_payment: deposit_installments_and_security gate payments_while_assessed ('Deposit payments are accepted only while the deposit is in assessed status.') satisfied by step 14 (prior_step DB delta on deposit_accounts.a0ce5ba0-f127-40c9-a1ce-a8cf8a0ba3cc); the gate installment_once is retired by the declared numbering overwrite. No time eligibility gate governs these four subjects, so temporal_feasibility is []. Boundary reasoning that still matters: the review window counts MONTHS(posting, 2026-10-07) < 24, so the 2024-09-05 charge (25 months) is out and 2025-11-05 is in; the interest year counts MONTHS < 12 so a payment on 2025-10-07 would belong to the previous year.

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. One customer, one agreement 8ec3baac-2560-49a2-ab1f-858fbe3a542a (Schedule GD, start 2019-06-03), one deposit a0ce5ba0-f127-40c9-a1ce-a8cf8a0ba3cc. Rows aggregated: deposit_transactions ca7efaaa-f54a-415e-b703-abd87a0068e9 (payment 10617.00, installment 1), 6b1b34ec-1a43-43b1-804a-a54fad93ffd9 (interest 422.60, period end 2025-10-07), 3ac7ac44-2b20-4abf-ae4b-b97862441c6a (excess refund 4832.00 by check, 2025-10-07). Service rows read: 36 regular bills, 6 late payment charges (2024-04-05, 2024-09-05 pre-window; 2025-11-05 waived by the courtesy credit posted 2025-11-07 with source_reference_id = that charge; 2025-12-06, 2026-02-05, 2026-07-06 counted), 36 payments (autopay from 2026-08-01), one written notice 2026-07-23 (the past-due balance was paid on 2026-07-27 and the agreement shows active again with last_status_date 2026-07-27). Excluded: pre-window late charges for the 24-month and 12-month counts; the waived charge (deducted); the 2025 excess refund is not a payment.

6. FACTOR CARD (tier taken / evidence / baseline figure from the Step 5 run; result moves for every factor).
 Extension = 2: shortfall_length 6 (3 counted vs allowance 2, no reversal; baseline 12 -> 8); clean_run_credit 3 months (latest charge 2026-07-06, 3 whole months; baseline 0 -> 5); notice_months +1 (notice 2026-07-23; baseline 0 -> 1); autopay_months -1 (3 autopay payments in 6 months; baseline 0 -> 3); service_length_months -1 (88 months; baseline 0 -> 3). All baselines at once: 12. Multi-source: shortfall_length (disconnection OR returned; late-over-one AND no returned). Near-miss: the 2025-11-05 charge is in the window but waived — counting it gives 4 (over by two) and the fall-through length 12.
 Interest = 119.61: opening_year_rate 0.0402 (year began 2025; baseline 0.0417 -> 120.62); calendar_year_split 85 days at 0.0402 + 280 at 0.0417 (baseline whole year at 0.0417 -> 120.62); interest_cash_base 5785.00 after the 4832.00 excess refund (baseline 10617.00 -> 219.51); satisfactory_months 6 (3 counted lapses; baseline 12 -> 239.21). All baselines: 442.73. Near-miss: the waived charge would make 4 lapses, same tier; the 2025-10-07 excess refund date equals the year start (a reader who drops it uses 10617.00).
 Recalculated requirement = 13694.00: recent_load_basis 7020.11 (3-month mean > 1.25 x 5074.95 and demand 368 kW > 273.5 kW; baseline 12-month mean -> 15225.00); payment_record_multiple 3.0 (baseline 2.5 -> 11939.00); service_length_cut 0.25 (baseline 0 -> 14572.00); notice_multiple_load 0.25 (baseline 0 -> 12817.00); growth_phase_in 0.5 (rise 14733.12 > 1.0 x held 6327.21; baseline 1 -> 21061.00). All baselines: 12688.00.
 Installment = 2946.70: interest_toward_raise held basis 6327.21 (24 months secured, no reversal; baseline held cash -> 3163.60); plan_size_count 3 (7366.79 >= 5785.00; baseline 1 -> 4911.18); autopay_extra_installments +1 (baseline 0 -> 3683.38); service_extra_installments +1 (baseline 0 -> 3683.38); front_loaded_installment 2.0 (notice in 12 months; baseline 1 -> 1473.35). All baselines: 7909.00.
 Cross-difficulty: every factor reading service records (shortfall_length, clean_run_credit, notice_months, autopay_months, service_length_months, satisfactory_months, recent_load_basis, payment_record_multiple, service_length_cut, notice_multiple_load, interest_toward_raise, plan_size_count, autopay_extra_installments, service_extra_installments, front_loaded_installment) is decided from the service_billing_and_collections product's ledger, seeded for this customer. No stamp decides any tier: held_amount on the deposit is a cache (6207.60) that the computations never read; they sum the ledger.

7. OVERRIDES (no second product law). Each new factor names the base sentence it replaces: extension -> 'A failed review leaves the deposit held and moves the refund review date out by review_extension_months.'; interest -> the rate sentence, the 'never compounded ... cash received' sentence and the anniversary/part-year crediting sentence of deposit_interest_rule; recalculation -> 'Business deposits are recalculated every recalculation_frequency_months after the fully secured date with the same formula as at assessment.'; installment -> the regular-installment sentence and the installment-number sentence. Everything else (threshold, due days, held-status gate, assessed-status gate, review allowances) is inherited. Base params values are unchanged; new constants live in each policy's params.

8. SEED DESIGN. Bills are priced by the GD tariff (customer charge 68.00, energy 0.08547/0.09104, demand 11.84 per billing kW with the 0.6 ratchet and 25 kW minimum, PSCR 0.00387) from chosen kWh and kW: 2023-10..2024-09 ~4247 (assessment basis 4246.55 -> 2.5 x = 10617), 2024-10..2025-09 ~3305 (2025 recalc basis 3305.37 x 1.75 = 5785), 2025-10..2026-02 ~3380 and growth from 2026-03 to ~7000 (second line). Late charges are 2%% of the unpaid bill posted on due + 4 days (grace 3); the 2025-11-05 charge meets the courtesy test (no late charge or reversal in the 12 months before it) and is waived on 2025-11-07. The 2026-07-23 written notice follows the June bill 20 days past due (>= 500.00), and the past-due balance is paid on 2026-07-27, the agreement showing active again with last_status_date 2026-07-27. Autopay starts with the July bill. The 2025 interest credit and the 2025 excess refund were generated with the extended laws on the as-of-2025 world, so history teaches the charter's algorithm. No automatic clause is lit beyond the four problems: the interest credit of year 2 and the recalculation are exactly the obligations of this tree; no outage, arrangement or other product holding exists.

9. PERSONA DESIGN. Margit Oyelaran, controller, brisk and organised. Volunteered: the deposit paid two years ago (seeded payment 2024-10-07), bills roughly doubled since spring (bills 2026-03.. ~2x), and the goal 'pay whatever part of it is due, today, on this call' with authority to let the representative record what the rules require and to pay herself. Given only when asked: phone 6164307259 (finder), EIN last four 5138 (verification), email or ZIP as spares. Passive reactions bound to the representative's utterances: review pushed back -> takes it in stride (late payments during the expansion); interest added -> good; surety bond / letter of credit offered -> keeps cash; funding source asked -> operating account; requirement going up -> asks how much is due today and accepts the plan; hand-over -> pays exactly as set out; receipt -> thanks and ends. She never names an amount, a count or a step, never mentions review/interest/recalculation first, and her last reaction answers the last gold action (the payment receipt).

10. REACHABILITY WALK. Turn 1 goal -> agent locates by phone (step 0), verifies phone + EIN (step 1, K=2), reads agreement, deposit, ledger, charges, credits, notices, bills (steps 2-8). From the extension policy and the records the agent decides the review is not passed and computes 2 months (step 10, agent). The interest policy's prerequisite sentence is now satisfied (review date 2026-12-07 > 2026-10-07): it credits 119.61 (step 12). The recalculation policy's sentence is satisfied (credit for 2026-10-07 on file): it records 13694.00 / 7020.11 / due 2026-10-17 (step 14). The installment policy's sentence is satisfied (assessed with raised requirement): the agent works out installment 2 of 5 = 2946.70, unlocks the user tool and hands it over (step 15); the customer calls it (step 16) and the receipt enters the transcript. Everything runs under frozen_time 2026-10-07 10:40 EDT; no wait, delivery, clearing or batch is assumed.

11. PLACES EASILY GOT WRONG. Counting the waived charge (4 instead of 3) -> wrong length and wrong interest months; skipping the review and crediting interest first (blocked by the interest sentence); computing the recalculation on the 12-month mean or without the phase-in; using held cash instead of held cash plus interest for the installment basis (24 months secured); forgetting autopay / service-length extra installments; treating the deposit's held_amount cache (6207.60) as current after the interest credit (computations read the ledger).

12. VERIFICATION. Authoring scripts (deleted after use) evaluated each policy compute with check_compute.build_env/eval_compute on the handling-time world (initial_state plus earlier gold writes replayed with the real tools). Output: extension_months 2 (factors 8/5/1/3/3, all-baseline 12); interest_amount 119.61 (120.62/120.62/219.51/239.21; 442.73); required_amount 13694.0 (15225/11939/14572/12817/21061; 12688); amount 2946.70 (3163.6/4911.18/3683.38/3683.38/1473.35; 7909.0). Edge deletion: P without R -> 0.0; R without I -> 13634.0; terminal review date without V -> 2026-10-07. Gates run: check_extended --task 0 EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK (17 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous); check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute COMPUTE OK (4 comps, 19 factors, 15 cross-difficulty, history rows 11, branches 89); check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK.

13. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. With compute/expected masked, reading only the rule prose of the four policies, the tool docstrings, the persona's lines and the finder returns gives the same answers: the review window counts 3 lapses -> length 6, credit 3, +1, -1, -1 = 2; the year's interest 5785.00 x (85 x 0.0402 + 280 x 0.0417)/365 x 6/12 = 119.61; the recalculated requirement ceil(6327.21 + (7020.11 x 3.0 - 6327.21) x 0.5) = 13694; the installment 2 x floor((13694.00 - 6327.21)/5 to the cent) = 2946.70, installment number 2, count 5. No second reading was found: the order is fixed by the three prerequisite sentences, the courtesy-waiver deduction is stated in every count, and each tier condition names its window.

14. CLOSURE. policy -> tool -> computation step -> GT call -> terminal: extension -> extend_deposit_review_04d6c850 -> step 10 -> refund_review_date 2026-12-07; interest -> credit_deposit_interest_e2c6de3a -> step 12 -> interest credit 119.61 / held 6327.21; recalculation -> require_additional_deposit_b541b477 -> step 14 -> status assessed, required 13694.00, due 2026-10-17; installment -> pay_additional_deposit_64b1dc0d -> step 16 -> payment 2946.70 as installment 2 of 5, held 9273.91. charter_scope.extended_policies = required_documents = computations' policy ids = the four problems; task_tools in first-call order. solvability_contract: steps 10/12/14 are state_due obligations evidenced by initial_state (review date, anniversary, recalculation date), step 16 is the customer's request; base gates evidenced pre-action (held status from initial_state; assessed status from the step 14 delta).

15. REVISION LOG. (a) Symptom: while building task 1, the payment-record multiple of the recalculation (fixed 3.0 / 2.0 / kind multiple) collapsed onto the fall-through for kinds whose own multiple is 2.0, and the single-lapse extension (fixed 6) equalled the residential review_extension_months; root cause: absolute tier values; change: tiers made relative to the kind (deposit multiple plus poor_record_load / less clean_record_relief; single_lapse_share 0.5 of review_extension_months; the additional plan counts installment_count_max plus count_large_extra / count_moderate_extra); re-run: every task 0 value unchanged (2, 119.61, 13694.00, 2946.70) and all per-task gates green. (b) Symptom: the installment-number dedup gate of the base could not be evidenced for a new number; change: declared numbering overwrite in the additional-installment policy; re-run SOLVABILITY OK. (c) Symptom: empty-string foreign keys flagged as dangling by replay; change: optional references seeded as null; re-run REPLAY OK.

16. REVISION LOG, ROUND 2 (policy-task audit security_deposits). Symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run:
 F-G1: the interest policy assigned 1 January to two rates (calendar-year rate sentence vs the split sentence counted with the start day excluded); the split sentence now reads 'its days up to and including 31 December of that earlier year earn the earlier year's rate and its days from 1 January of the anniversary's year on earn the closing year's rate', and compute days_prior_year = MX(0, DAYS(year_start, 1 January) - 1). Re-run: 85 days at 0.0402 + 280 at 0.0417, period rate 0.0413506849, interest 119.61 (was 119.59); the seeded first-year credit was re-derived under the same law, 422.60 (was 422.55), held_amount 6207.60; recalculation still 13694.00 (phased 13693.77 on held 6327.21); additional installment 2946.70 (due 7366.79, regular 1473.35); edge deletions unchanged in kind (13634.00 without the interest credit, 0.00 without the recalculation).
 F-G2: the recalculation policy now states 'The billing basis so chosen, rounded to the cent, is the average monthly bill recorded on the deposit with the recalculated requirement.' (step 14 average_monthly_bill 7020.11 now has a policy sentence).
 F-G4: the additional-installment policy declares an overwrite of deposit_recalculation's 'When the recalculated amount exceeds the held cash ... and the difference due within additional_deposit_due_days.' replaced by 'Where a recalculation has returned the deposit to assessed with a raised required amount, the difference due within additional_deposit_due_days is this additional amount due, the held basis taking the place of the held cash.'
 F-G5: the calendar-year split's baseline is now the closing year's rate (closing_rate), and the baseline paragraph states the Commission's year schedule and 'the Commission's deposit interest rate for the calendar year of the anniversary', so the fall-through tier equals the baseline in every year; figures unchanged here (120.62).
 O-G2: the extension measures every window on 'the decision day, the day on which the review is decided'; the interest policy states that the year's payments and lapses are counted over the 12 months ending on the day the credit is booked. O-G4: the additional-installment policy states the later installments (equal shares, last carries the remainder, 30 days apart). O-G7: tool docstrings no longer say 'after its review' or 'so that the additional amount can be paid'. O-G8: edge conditions say 'the day the credit is booked' and 'the recalculation date'. O-G11: the additional-installment policy declares an overwrite of the base fully-secured sentence: a re-assessed deposit becomes held again when its held basis reaches the raised requirement. O-G1, O-G3, O-G10 kept as documented (blueprint claim list frozen; the disconnection count is used only in '> 0' tests and the rule states the compute's count; the waiver deduction is this policy's own stated count).
 Gates after the round: full block re-run (see final report).

17. REVISION LOG, ROUND 3 (policy-task audit revision_2; this task passed and is unchanged in world, persona, writes and values). Charter edits touching this task's policies: N-1 — the additional-installment overwrite of deposit_recalculation now restates the threshold in its replacement sentence ('When a recalculated amount exceeds the held cash by more than recalculation_increase_threshold_pct of the held cash, the deposit returns to assessed with the raised required amount, and the difference due ... is this additional amount due, the held basis taking the place of the held cash.'); here 13694.00 clears the threshold against both 5785.00 and 6327.21. N-2 — the held-trigger overwrite now restates the general base trigger and carves out the re-assessed deposit. N-3 — opening_year_rate's baseline is now closing_rate (bindings reordered so closing_rate precedes prior_year_rate); on this 2026 anniversary closing_rate is 0.0417, so the factor figure stays 120.62. Re-run: gold 2 / 119.61 / 13694.00 / 2946.70 and every sensitivity figure unchanged.
